thread:
maria: Heads-up — saw a CPU spike on the telemetry pipeline ~09:12 UTC, coincident with a 3x increase in span ingest. P99 exporter latency jumped and collector CPU went from ~20% to ~72% on the 4x worker nodes.

telemetry-bot: [alert] otel-collector.cpu > 60% for 3m (service=telemetry-collector, env=prod) :rotating_light:

jong: Which exporter? gRPC or OTLP/HTTP? Any indication of backpressure (queue drops)?

maria: gRPC -> internal exporter -> s3-archiver. Queue length on the exporter buffer spiked, then exporter started retrying. No obvious network errors, CPU looks spent in attribute processing and span serialization.

akshay: Do we have span size distribution? high-cardinality attributes can kill CPU when copying/encoding JSON.

maria: Quick sample: median span size 600 bytes, 95th ~4.2KB, but tail had many 20-40KB spans with 200+ attributes (user metadata).

lisa: Oof. Those 200+ attrs are likely from unfiltered HTTP headers or request context. We should consider dropping or hashing certain attributes before batching.

ben: Also check batching config. If the batch size is too small, overhead per RPC skyrockets. Current config: `send_batch_size: 512`, `send_batch_max_time: 200ms` on exporter.

jong: Proposed immediate mitigation: 1) enable attribute_filter processor to drop known noisy keys, 2) increase batch size to 2048 and max_time to 500ms, 3) run a canary on 10% of traffic. Any objections?

akshay: Agree. For attribute_filter rules, start with: `drop_keys: ["cookie", "authorization", "user_agent_full", "raw_headers"]` and `match_type: regexp` for anything like `^x-.*-meta`. Also consider `hash_keys` for ids we need for dedup but not raw values.

maria: I'll open a short-lived rollout PR and add a transform processor snippet: 
```yaml
processors:
  transform/reduce-attrs:
    actions:
      - key: "http.request.headers"
        action: "delete"
      - key: "user.email"
        action: "hash"
      - key: "request.raw_payload"
        action: "delete"
```

lisa: How about sampling? If those spans are mostly noise, probabilistic sampling on service=frontend could cut volume drastically. But we should be careful to keep traces for important requests.

maria: Right — sampling will affect downstream analytics. Plan: do attribute pruning + batching first, measure CPU and p99 exporter latency for 60m, then add targeted tail-sampling if needed.

ben: Can someone run a quick perf diff? Suggested experiment commands: `kubectl exec -c collector -- top -b -n1 | head -n20` and curl the /metrics endpoint: `curl -s http://collector:8888/metrics | grep exporter` to capture exporter queue length and send latencies.

maria: Running that now on a canary pod, posting results in ~10m.

telemetry-bot: [note] created incident ticket INF-4192 for telemetry CPU spike — assigned to @maria and @jong.

jong: If CPU still high after pruning + batching, we should consider adding a fast path for spans with <10 attrs to skip expensive attribute maps allocation. Might be a small runtime change but high ROI.

akshay: I can prototype a micro-optimization in the collector fork — pool attribute maps and avoid heap copies for common cases. Can we get perf / bench vectors?

maria: Thanks. Action items: (1) PR with attribute_filter + transform + batching tweak -> canary 10% (maria), (2) collect 60m metrics and p99 comparisons (lisa), (3) akshay prototype allocator micro-opt and bench (akshay), (4) follow-up meeting in #eng-platform 11:30 PT if numbers don't improve.

lisa: :thumbsup: I'll also add a quick dashboard tile for exporter_queue_length and exporter_send_latency.p99 so product folks can watch.

ben: Remember to add changelog note — transient change to batching may affect downstream consumer ingestion patterns.

maria: Will do. Posting PR link when ready.

jong: Great, thanks all. :eyes:
